title.en: Volume 88 Book of Later Jin 14: Biographies 3: Jing Yangguang, Li Yantao, Zhang Xichong, Wang Tingyin, Shi Kuanghan, Liang Hanyong, Yang Siquan, Yin Hui, Li Congzhang, Li Congwen, Zhang Wanjin
title.raw: 卷八十八 晉書14: 列傳三 景延廣 李彥韜 張希崇 王庭胤 史匡翰 梁漢顒 楊思權 尹暉 李從璋 李從溫 張萬進 Volume 88 Book of Later Jin 14: Biographies 3: Jing Yangguang, Li Yantao, Zhang Xichong, Wang Tingyin, Shi Kuanghan, Liang Hanyong, Yang Siquan, Yin Hui, Li Congzhang, Li Congwen, Zhang Wanjin

sentences.zh: 景延廣，字航川，陜州人也。

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang, courtesy name Hangchuan, was a native of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang, whose courtesy name was Hangchuan, came from Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父建，累贈太尉。

translations.literal: His father Jian was posthumously promoted several times to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian received successive posthumous promotions culminating in the rank of Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 延廣少習射，以挽強見稱。

translations.literal: Yanguang studied archery in his youth and was renowned for drawing strong bows.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yanguang trained in archery and won fame for his strength at the bow.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，邵王朱友誨節制於陜，召置麾下，友誨坐謀亂，延廣竄而獲免。

translations.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang, Prince Shao Zhu Youhui held military command at Shan and summoned him into his service; Youhui was implicated in a plot, and Yanguang fled and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang's Kaiping era, Prince Shao Zhu Youhui commanded at Shan and took Yanguang into his staff. When Youhui was convicted of plotting rebellion, Yanguang fled and escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 後事華州連帥尹皓，皓引薦列校，隸於汴軍，從王彥章拒莊宗於河上。

translations.literal: Later he served Yin Hao, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture; Hao recommended him as a company commander, he was attached to the Bian army, and followed Wang Yanzhang in resisting Zhuangzong on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Yin Hao, the military commissioner of Hua Prefecture. Hao recommended him as a company commander and attached him to the Bian army, where he followed Wang Yanzhang in resisting Zhuangzong along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 及中都之敗，彥章見擒，而延廣被數創，歸於汴。

translations.literal: When Zhongdu fell, Yanzhang was captured while Yanguang suffered several wounds and returned to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Zhongdu, Yanzhang was taken prisoner while Yanguang, wounded several times, made his way back to Bian.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，明宗幸夷門，會朱守殷拒命，尋平之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang, Mingzong visited Yimen; Zhu Shouyin defied orders, and he was soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tiancheng era, Emperor Mingzong visited Yimen just as Zhu Shouyin rose in defiance; the revolt was soon put down.

sentences.zh: 延廣以軍校連坐，將棄市。

translations.literal: Yanguang was implicated as a military officer and was to be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was implicated as a company officer and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 高祖時為六軍副使，掌其事，見而惜之，乃密遣遁去，尋收為客將。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu was deputy commander of the Six Armies and oversaw the matter; seeing him, he took pity and secretly sent him to escape, then soon took him in as a guest general.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, then deputy commander of the Six Armies and in charge of the case, took pity on him and secretly let him escape; he soon took Yanguang on as a guest general.

sentences.zh: 及張敬達之圍晉陽，高祖付以戎事，甚有幹城之功。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu entrusted him with military affairs, and he rendered great service in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu put him in charge of the defense, and he distinguished himself in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，授侍衛步軍都指揮使、檢校司徒，遙領果州團練使，轉檢校太保，領夔州節度使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army, Acting Minister of Works, titular military commissioner of Guo Prefecture, then Acting Grand Guardian, and military commissioner of Kui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Yanguang was made Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army and Acting Minister of Works, with a titular commission as military commissioner of Guo Prefecture; he was later promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and given the Kui prefectural command.

sentences.zh: 四年，出鎮滑臺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out to command at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posted to command at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 五年，加檢校太傅，移鎮陜府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional title Acting Grand Tutor and transferred to command at Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor and was transferred to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，召為侍衛馬步都虞候，移鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Chief Inspector of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, and transferred to command at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled as Chief Inspector of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot and reassigned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉侍衛親軍都指揮使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Commander of the Palace Guard Personal Army and Acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Commander of the Palace Guard Personal Army and Acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，高祖晏駕，延廣與宰臣馮道等承顧命，以少帝為嗣。

translations.literal: That summer Gaozu died; Yanguang with the chief minister Feng Dao and others received the dying command and installed the Young Emperor as successor.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when Gaozu died, Yanguang joined Chief Minister Feng Dao and others in carrying out the dying command to install the Young Emperor as heir.

sentences.zh: 既發喪，都人不得偶語，百官赴臨，未及內門，皆令下馬，由是有驕暴之失。

translations.literal: Once mourning was proclaimed, the capital's people were forbidden to speak together; officials coming to mourn were made to dismount before reaching the inner gate—hence he incurred the fault of arrogance and brutality.
translations.idiomatic: Once mourning was proclaimed, people in the capital were forbidden even to speak together in passing, and officials coming to mourn were ordered to dismount before they reached the inner gate. From this he earned a reputation for arrogance and brutality.

sentences.zh: 少帝既嗣位，延廣獨以為己功，尋加同平章事，彌有矜伐之色。

translations.literal: After the Young Emperor succeeded, Yanguang alone regarded it as his achievement; he was soon made Associate Grand Councilor and showed ever more self-congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: After the Young Emperor took the throne, Yanguang alone claimed the succession as his doing. He was soon made Associate Grand Councilor and grew ever more boastful.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使告哀契丹，無表致書，去臣稱孫。

translations.literal: The court sent envoys to announce mourning to Khitan; there was no memorial, only a letter, and the status of subject was dropped in favor of calling themselves grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to announce Gaozu's death to the Khitan, but sent a letter rather than a formal memorial and dropped the language of subjecthood, styling themselves only as grandson.

sentences.zh: 契丹怒，遣使來讓，延廣乃奏令契丹回國使喬榮

translations.literal: Khitan was angered and sent envoys to reproach them; Yanguang then memorialized ordering the Khitan return-envoy Qiao Rong
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were furious and sent envoys to protest. Yanguang then memorialized that the Khitan return-envoy Qiao Rong

sentences.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：先是，河陽牙將喬榮從趙延壽入遼，遼帝以為回國使，置邸大梁。

translations.literal: (Khitan State Annals: Earlier, Heyang staff officer Qiao Rong had followed Zhao Yanshou into Liao; the Liao emperor made him return-envoy and established a residence at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: (Khitan State Annals: Earlier, Qiao Rong, a staff officer at Heyang, had followed Zhao Yanshou into Liao, and the Liao emperor appointed him return-envoy with a residence at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 至是，景延廣說帝囚榮於獄，凡遼國販易在晉境者，皆殺之，奪其貨。

translations.literal: At this time Jing Yanguang persuaded the emperor to imprison Rong in jail; all Liao traders within Jin territory were killed and their goods seized.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jing Yanguang persuaded the emperor to throw Rong in prison, and every Liao trader in Jin territory was killed and his goods seized.

sentences.zh: 大臣皆言遼國不可負，乃釋榮，慰賜而遣之。）〉

translations.literal: The chief ministers all said Liao could not be wronged, so Rong was released, comforted with gifts, and sent away.))〉
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all warned that Liao must not be provoked, so Rong was released, given gifts and comfort, and sent home.))〉

sentences.zh: 告戎王曰：「先帝則北朝所立，今上則中國自策，為鄰為孫則可，無臣之理。」

translations.literal: to tell the barbarian king: "The late emperor was installed by the northern court; the present sovereign was enthroned by China itself—as neighbor and grandson that may do, but there is no ground for subjecthood."
translations.idiomatic: He should tell the Khitan ruler: "The late emperor was enthroned by your northern court, but the present sovereign was raised up by China itself. We may be neighbors and you may call us grandson, but there is no basis for subjecthood."

sentences.zh: 且言：「晉朝有十萬口橫磨劍，翁若要戰則早來，他日不禁孫子，則取笑天下，當成後悔矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "The Jin court has a hundred thousand mouths sharpening swords on the grindstone—if the old man wants battle, let him come early; if later he cannot restrain his grandson, he will be laughed at by all under heaven and surely regret it."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Jin court has a hundred thousand men whetting swords on the grindstone. If you want a fight, old man, come soon. If you cannot keep your grandson in line later, the world will laugh at you—and you will regret it."

sentences.zh: 由是與契丹立敵，干戈日尋。

translations.literal: From this they became enemies with Khitan, and arms were sought day by day.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jin and Khitan became enemies, and war drew nearer day by day.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖在位時，宣借楊光遠騎兵數百，延廣請下詔遣還，光遠由此忿延廣，怨朝廷，遣使泛海構釁。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Gaozu was on the throne, he had borrowed several hundred cavalry from Yang Guangyuan; Yanguang asked that an edict be issued to return them, and Guangyuan hence resented Yanguang, blamed the court, and sent envoys across the sea to stir trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Gaozu still reigned, the court had borrowed several hundred horsemen from Yang Guangyuan. Yanguang urged an edict ordering their return. Guangyuan thereupon hated Yanguang, turned against the court, and sent envoys by sea to provoke conflict.

sentences.zh: 天福八年十二月，契丹乃南牧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Tianfu, Khitan then drove their herds south.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianfu 8, the Khitan drove south in force.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，陷甘陵，河北儲蓄悉在其郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year they took Ganling; all stores of Hebei were within that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year they captured Ganling, and all of Hebei's stored supplies fell into their hands.

sentences.zh: 少帝大駭，親率六師，進駐澶淵。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor was greatly alarmed, personally led the Six Armies, and advanced to encamp at Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor was terrified and personally led the Six Armies forward to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 延廣為上將，凡六師進退，皆出胸臆，少帝亦不能制，眾鹹憚而忌之。

translations.literal: Yanguang was supreme commander; all advances and retreats of the Six Armies came from his breast alone—the Young Emperor also could not control him, and all feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang served as supreme commander. Every movement of the Six Armies came from his own judgment alone, and even the Young Emperor could not restrain him. The army both feared and resented him.

sentences.zh: 契丹既至城下，使人宣言曰：「景延廣喚我來相殺，何不急戰！」

translations.literal: When Khitan reached below the walls, they sent someone to proclaim: "Jing Yanguang summoned us to come kill each other—why not fight quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan reached the walls, their envoy proclaimed: "Jing Yanguang called us here to kill each other—why not fight at once!"

sentences.zh: 一日，高行周與蕃軍相遇於近郊，以眾寡不敵，急請濟師，延廣勒兵不出，是日行周幸而獲免。

translations.literal: One day Gao Xingzhou met the barbarian army in the near suburbs; outnumbered, he urgently requested reinforcements, but Yanguang held the troops and would not go out—that day Xingzhou luckily escaped.
translations.idiomatic: One day Gao Xingzhou clashed with the Khitan army in the suburbs. Outnumbered, he urgently asked for reinforcements, but Yanguang held his troops back. That day Xingzhou escaped only by luck.

sentences.zh: 及契丹退，延廣猶閉柵自固，士大夫曰：「昔與契丹絕好，言何勇也；

translations.literal: When Khitan withdrew, Yanguang still closed the palisade and held himself secure; scholar-officials said: "In the past when breaking with Khitan, how brave his words;
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Khitan withdrew, Yanguang kept the palisades shut and held his position. Scholar-officials remarked: "When he broke with the Khitan, how bold his words were;

sentences.zh: 今契丹至若是，氣何憊也。」

translations.literal: now that Khitan has come like this, how exhausted his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: yet now that they have actually come, how spent his courage is.

sentences.zh: 時延廣在軍，母兇問至，自澶淵津北移於津南，不信宿而復蒞戎事，曾無戚容，下里之士亦聞而惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Yanguang was in the army; news of his mother's death arrived; he moved from north of the Chanyuan ford to south of the ford, and within less than a night's lodging returned to military affairs without a trace of grief—even common folk heard and detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was then in camp when word came that his mother had died. He moved his quarters from the north bank of the Chanyuan ford to the south bank, and within a day was back at his military duties without a sign of mourning. Even common people heard of it and despised him.

sentences.zh: 時有太常丞王緒者，因使德州回，與延廣有隙，因誣奏與楊光遠通謀，遣吏縶於麾下，鍛成其事。

translations.literal: There was then Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Wang Xu, returning from an envoy mission to Dezhou; he had a rift with Yanguang, who on a false charge memorialized that Xu conspired with Yang Guangyuan, sent officers to bind him under his command, and forged the case to completion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Xu, a vice director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, was returning from an envoy mission to Dezhou. He and Yanguang had a grudge, and Yanguang falsely accused him of plotting with Yang Guangyuan, had him seized under his command, and fabricated the case to the end.

sentences.zh: 判官盧億累勸解不從，尋有詔棄市，時甚冤之。

translations.literal: Judge-advocate Lu Yi repeatedly urged release but was not heeded; soon there was an edict for execution in the marketplace, and at the time it was greatly deemed unjust.
translations.idiomatic: His judge-advocate Lu Yi repeatedly urged mercy, but Yanguang would not listen. An edict soon ordered Xu executed in the marketplace, and many regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 少帝還京，嘗幸其第，進獻錫賚，有如酬酢，權寵恩渥，為一朝之冠。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor returned to the capital, he once visited his residence; gifts and rewards were presented back and forth like toasts, and his power, favor, and grace exceeded all others of the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor returned to the capital, he visited Yanguang's mansion. Gifts and rewards passed back and forth like toasts at a feast. His power and favor stood at the summit of the court.

sentences.zh: 俄與宰臣桑維翰不協，少帝亦憚其難制，遂罷兵權，出為洛都留守、兼侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he fell out with Chief Minister Sang Weihan; the Young Emperor also feared he was hard to control, so his military authority was removed and he went out as Luoyang garrison commander, concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon clashed with Chief Minister Sang Weihan, and the Young Emperor also feared he could not be controlled. Yanguang was stripped of military command and sent out as garrison commander of Luoyang, with the concurrent title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 由是郁郁不得志，亦意契丹強盛，國家不濟，身將危矣，但縱長夜飲，無復以夾輔為意。

translations.literal: Hence he was depressed and unfulfilled; he also thought Khitan strong, the state failing, and himself soon in peril—he only indulged in drinking through long nights and no longer thought of aiding the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he brooded in frustration. He also judged the Khitan too strong, the state doomed, and his own life in peril. He drank through the long nights and no longer gave thought to serving the throne.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史·盧多遜傳》：父億。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Lu Duosun: His father was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Lu Duosun: His father was Yi.

sentences.zh: 景延廣鎮天平，表億掌書記，留守西洛，又為判官。

translations.literal: When Jing Yanguang commanded Tianping, he recommended Yi as secretary; garrisoning western Luoyang, he also made him judge-advocate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Yanguang held Tianping, he recommended Yi as secretary. When Yanguang garrisoned western Luoyang, Yi also served as his judge-advocate.

sentences.zh: 時國用窘乏，取民財以助軍。

translations.literal: At the time state funds were strained and lacking; the people's wealth was taken to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: State funds were then exhausted, and the government took money from the people to support the army.

sentences.zh: 河南府計出二十萬緡，延廣欲並緣以圖羨利，增為三十七萬緡。

translations.literal: Henan Prefecture was assessed at two hundred thousand strings of cash; Yanguang wished to use the occasion for extra profit and raised it to three hundred seventy thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture was assessed at two hundred thousand strings of cash. Yanguang wanted to profit from the levy and raised the figure to three hundred seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 億諫曰：「公位兼將相，既富且貴，今國帑空竭，不得已而取資於民，公何忍利之乎！」

translations.literal: Yi remonstrated: "Your lordship holds both general and minister rank, already rich and noble; now the state treasury is empty and exhausted—we take from the people only because we must—how can your lordship bear to profit from it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "You hold both military and civil rank and are already wealthy and exalted. The treasury is empty and the state takes from the people only because it must. How can you bear to profit from that?"

sentences.zh: 延廣慚而止。）〉

translations.literal: Yanguang was ashamed and stopped.))〉
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was ashamed and desisted.))〉

sentences.zh: 開運三年冬，契丹渡滹水。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun, Khitan crossed the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Kaiyun 3, the Khitan crossed the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 詔遣屯孟津，將戒途，由府署正門而出，所乘馬騰立不進，幾墜於地，乃易乘而行，時以為不祥之甚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to encamp at Mengjin; about to set out on the road, he went out through the main gate of the prefectural office; the horse he rode reared and would not advance, nearly throwing him to the ground, so he changed mounts and went—at the time this was deemed a very ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to encamp at Mengjin. As he was about to depart, he left through the main gate of the prefectural office, but his horse reared and refused to move, nearly throwing him. He changed horses and went on, and many took this as a dire omen.

sentences.zh: 及王師降契丹，延廣狼狽而還。

translations.literal: When the royal army surrendered to Khitan, Yanguang returned in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army surrendered to the Khitan, Yanguang fled home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 時契丹主至安陽，遣別部隊長率騎士數千，與晉兵相雜，趨河橋入洛，以取延廣。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan ruler reached Anyang and sent a detached unit leader with several thousand horsemen, mingled with Jin troops, to hurry to the river bridge and enter Luoyang to seize Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler had reached Anyang and sent a detached commander with several thousand horsemen, mixed in with Jin soldiers, to rush the river bridge into Luoyang and seize Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 戒曰：「如延廣奔吳走蜀，便當追而致之。」

translations.literal: He warned: "If Yanguang flees to Wu or runs to Shu, pursue and bring him in."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed them: "If Yanguang flees to Wu or Shu, pursue him and bring him back."

sentences.zh: 時延廣顧慮其家，未能引決。

translations.literal: At the time Yanguang thought of his family and could not bring himself to suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was then thinking of his family and could not bring himself to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 契丹既奄至，乃與從事閻丕輕騎謁契丹主於封丘，與丕俱見縶焉。

translations.literal: When Khitan suddenly arrived, he then went with staff member Yan Pi on light horses to call on the Khitan ruler at Fengqiu, and both Pi and he were bound.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan suddenly arrived, he rode with his staff member Yan Pi to meet the Khitan ruler at Fengqiu. Both men were seized.

sentences.zh: 〈（《遼史》：將軍康祥執景延廣來獻。）〉

translations.literal: (Liao History: General Kang Xiang seized Jing Yanguang and presented him.))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Liao History: General Kang Xiang seized Jing Yanguang and presented him as a captive.))〉

sentences.zh: 延廣曰：「丕，臣之從事也，以職相隨，何罪而亦為縲囚？」

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "Pi is my staff member who followed me in duty—what crime has he that he too should be a bound prisoner?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said: "Pi is only my staff officer who followed me in duty. What crime has he committed that he too should be bound?"

sentences.zh: 契丹釋之。

translations.literal: Khitan released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan released him.

sentences.zh: 因責延廣曰：「致南北失歡，良由爾也。」

translations.literal: They then reproached Yanguang: "You caused North and South to lose harmony—truly because of you."
translations.idiomatic: They then rebuked Yanguang: "You are the one who destroyed harmony between north and south."

sentences.zh: 乃召喬榮質證前事，凡有十焉。

translations.literal: They then summoned Qiao Rong to verify the earlier matters—there were ten in all.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Qiao Rong to testify about the earlier affair. There were ten counts in all.

sentences.zh: 始榮將入蕃時，紿延廣云：「某恐忽忘所達之語，請紀於翰墨。」

translations.literal: When Rong was first about to enter the barbarian lands, he deceived Yanguang saying: "I fear I may suddenly forget the words I am to convey—please record them in writing."
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was first about to return to Liao, he tricked Yanguang, saying: "I am afraid I may forget the message I am to deliver. Please write it down."

sentences.zh: 延廣信之，乃命吏備記其事。

translations.literal: Yanguang believed him and ordered clerks to prepare a full record of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang believed him and ordered a clerk to write everything down.

sentences.zh: 榮亦憸巧善事人者也，慮他日見詰，則執之以取信，因匿其文於衣中。

translations.literal: Rong was also crafty and skilled at pleasing people; fearing interrogation another day, he would hold the document to gain credence, and so hid the text in his clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was crafty and skilled at currying favor. Fearing future questioning, he kept the document as proof and hid it in his clothes.

sentences.zh: 至是，延廣始以他語抗對，榮乃出其文以質之，延廣頓為所屈。

translations.literal: At this point Yanguang at first answered with other words in resistance; Rong then produced his text to confront him, and Yanguang was suddenly overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yanguang tried to answer with other words, but Rong produced the written record. Yanguang was instantly silenced.

sentences.zh: 每服一事，則受牙籌一莖，此契丹法也。

translations.literal: For each matter he conceded, he received one tally stick—this was Khitan law.
translations.idiomatic: For each count he admitted, he received one tally stick. That was Khitan custom.

sentences.zh: 延廣受至八莖，但以面伏地，契丹遂咄之，命鎖延廣臂，將送之北土。

translations.literal: Yanguang received up to eight sticks, then only lay face down on the ground; Khitan then shouted at him and ordered Yanguang's arms bound, intending to send him to the northern land.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang received eight sticks, then lay face down on the ground. The Khitan shouted at him, ordered his arms bound, and prepared to send him north.

sentences.zh: 是日，至於陳橋民家草舍，延廣懼燔灼之害，至夜分伺守者怠，則引手自扼其吭，尋卒焉。

translations.literal: That day, reaching a commoner's thatched hut at Chenqiao, Yanguang feared the harm of burning; at midnight he watched until the guards slackened, then drew his hand to throttle his throat, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: That day they reached a peasant's thatched hut at Chenqiao. Fearing he would be burned alive, Yanguang waited until midnight, when the guards grew careless, and strangled himself. He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 雖事已窮頓，人亦壯之，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Although matters had reached utter extremity, people also admired his spirit; he was then fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Though his end was desperate, many admired his final act. He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：昝居潤嘗為樞密院小吏，景延廣留守西京，補為右職。

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Affairs Outline: Zan Jurun had once been a minor clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs; when Jing Yanguang garrisoned the western capital, he was appointed to a senior post.
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Affairs Outline: Zan Jurun had once been a minor clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs. When Jing Yanguang garrisoned the western capital, he appointed Jurun to a senior post.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，以兵圍延廣家。

translations.literal: When Khitan invaded the capital, they surrounded Yanguang's house with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded the capital, they surrounded Yanguang's house with troops.

sentences.zh: 故吏悉避去，居潤為全護其家，時論稱之。）〉

translations.literal: Former subordinates all fled; Jurun fully protected his household—contemporary opinion praised him.))〉
translations.idiomatic: All his former subordinates fled, but Jurun protected the household intact. Contemporary opinion praised him.))〉

sentences.zh: 漢高祖登極，詔贈中書令。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, an edict posthumously granted him Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延廣少時，嘗泛洞庭湖，中流阻風，帆裂舵折，眾大懼。

translations.literal: When Yanguang was young, he once sailed on Dongting Lake; midstream they were blocked by wind, sails torn and rudder broken, and all were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yanguang once sailed on Dongting Lake. Midstream a storm blocked them, tearing the sails and breaking the rudder, and everyone was terrified.

sentences.zh: 頃之，舟人指波中曰：「賢聖來護，此必有貴人矣。」

translations.literal: Shortly, the boatmen pointed into the waves and said: "Sages and worthies come to protect—there must be a noble person here."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the boatmen pointed into the waves and said: "Sages are coming to protect us. There must be a man of destiny aboard."

sentences.zh: 尋獲濟焉。

translations.literal: Soon they were able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: They soon made it safely ashore.

sentences.zh: 竟位至將相，非偶然也。

translations.literal: In the end he reached the rank of general and minister—it was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: That he rose in the end to general and minister was no accident.

sentences.zh: 李彥韜，太原人也。

translations.literal: Li Yantao was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yantao came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少事邢州節度使閻寶為皂隸，寶卒，高祖收於帳下。

translations.literal: In youth he served Xing Prefecture military commissioner Yan Bao as a menial; when Bao died, Gaozu took him into his retinue.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Yan Bao, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, as a menial servant. When Bao died, Gaozu took him into his household.

sentences.zh: 及起義，以少帝留守北京，因留彥韜為腹心。

translations.literal: When the uprising began, the Young Emperor was left to garrison Beijing, and Yantao was kept as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, the Young Emperor was left to hold Beijing, and Yantao was kept as his trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 歷客將、牙門都校，以纖巧故，厚承委用。

translations.literal: He passed through guest general and gate-guard commander; because of his subtle craftiness, he was heavily entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of guest general and gate-guard commander. Because of his subtle cleverness, he received heavy trust and wide responsibility.

sentences.zh: 及少帝嗣位，授蔡州刺史，入為內客省使、宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made prefect of Cai Prefecture, then entered the court as Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, Yantao was made prefect of Cai and then brought to court as Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遙領壽州節度，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保，俄改陳州節度使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: Before long he held titular command of Shou Prefecture, served as Commander of the Palace Guard Horse Army and Acting Grand Guardian, and soon became military commissioner of Chen Prefecture while continuing to command the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he held a titular commission as military commissioner of Shou, served as Commander of the Palace Guard Horse Army and Acting Grand Guardian, and soon became military commissioner of Chen while retaining command of the army.

sentences.zh: 每在帝側，升除將相，但與宦官近臣締結，致外情不通，陷君於危亡之地。

translations.literal: Always at the emperor's side, he rose to general and minister rank, but only formed ties with eunuchs and close attendants, causing outside sentiment not to reach the throne and plunging the ruler into peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Always at the emperor's side, he rose to the rank of general and minister, but he bonded only with eunuchs and intimate attendants. Outside opinion never reached the throne, and he helped drive the ruler toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「朝廷所設文官將何用也。」

translations.literal: He once told others: "What use are the civil officials the court establishes?"
translations.idiomatic: He once said to others: "What use are the civil officials the court keeps on its rolls?"

sentences.zh: 且欲澄汰而除廢之，則可知其輔弼之道也。

translations.literal: Moreover he wished to clarify and eliminate them—thus one may know his way of aiding the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He even wanted to purge and abolish them altogether, which shows what kind of counselor he was.

sentences.zh: 及契丹犯闕，遷少帝於開封府。

translations.literal: When Khitan violated the capital, the Young Emperor was moved to Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan stormed the capital, the Young Emperor was moved to the Kaifeng prefectural residence.

sentences.zh: 一日，少帝遣人急召彥韜，將與計事，彥韜辭不赴命，少帝怏恨久之，其負國辜君也如是。

translations.literal: One day the Young Emperor urgently summoned Yantao to consult on affairs; Yantao declined and did not answer the summons—the Young Emperor nursed resentment for a long time; his betrayal of state and wronging of the ruler were like this.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Young Emperor urgently summoned Yantao to consult on affairs. Yantao refused to come. The emperor brooded on it for a long time. That was how he betrayed his country and failed his ruler.

sentences.zh: 及少帝北遷，戎王遣彥韜從行，洎至蕃中，隸於國母帳下。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor was moved north, the barbarian king sent Yantao to accompany him; when they reached the barbarian lands, he was attached to the Queen Mother's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor was sent north, the Khitan ruler ordered Yantao to accompany him. In Liao territory he was placed under the Queen Mother's household.

sentences.zh: 永康王舉兵攻國母，以偉王為前鋒，國母發兵拒之，以彥韜為排陣使，彥韜降於偉王，偉王置之帳下，其後卒於幽州。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang raised troops to attack the Queen Mother, with Prince Wei as vanguard; the Queen Mother sent troops to resist, making Yantao battle-array officer—Yantao surrendered to Prince Wei, who placed him in his camp; he later died at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang raised troops against the Queen Mother and made Prince Wei his vanguard. The Queen Mother sent an army to resist and appointed Yantao battle-array officer. Yantao defected to Prince Wei, who took him into his camp. He later died at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 張希崇，字德峰，幽州薊縣人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xichong, courtesy name Defeng, was a native of Ji County in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xichong, whose courtesy name was Defeng, came from Ji County in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父行簡，假薊州玉田令。

translations.literal: His father Xingjian was acting magistrate of Yutian in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingjian served as acting magistrate of Yutian in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 希崇少通《左氏春秋》，復癖於吟詠。

translations.literal: Xichong in youth mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and was also devoted to composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Xichong mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and was devoted to poetry.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，劉守光為燕帥，性慘酷，不喜儒士，希崇乃擲筆以自效，守光納之，漸升為裨將。

translations.literal: In the Tianyou era Liu Shouguang was Yan commander; his nature was cruel and harsh, disliking scholar-gentlemen—Xichong then cast aside the brush to offer his service, Shouguang took him in, and he gradually rose to deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianyou era Liu Shouguang commanded Yan. Cruel by nature and hostile to scholars, Xichong laid aside his brush and offered military service. Shouguang took him in, and he gradually rose to deputy general.

sentences.zh: 俄而守光敗，唐莊宗命周德威鎮其地，希崇以舊籍列於麾下，尋遣率偏師守平州。

translations.literal: Soon Shouguang was defeated; Tang Zhuangzong ordered Zhou Dewei to garrison the region; Xichong by old registration was listed under his command, and soon was sent to lead a detached force garrisoning Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang was soon defeated, and Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei to garrison the region. Xichong, by virtue of his earlier service, was placed under Zhou's command and soon sent to lead a detached force holding Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安巴堅南攻，陷其城，掠希崇而去。

translations.literal: Ambaqian attacked south, took the city, and carried Xichong off.
translations.idiomatic: Ambaqian attacked from the south, captured the city, and carried Xichong off as a captive.

sentences.zh: 阿保機詢希崇，乃知其儒人也，因授元帥府判官，後遷盧龍軍行軍司馬，繼改蕃漢都提舉使。

translations.literal: Abaoji questioned Xichong and thus knew he was a scholar-gentleman; he therefore appointed him judge-advocate of the Marshal's Office, later promoted him to Luolong Army campaigning deputy, and then changed him to Commissioner for Overseeing All Barbarian and Han Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji questioned Xichong and learned that he was a scholar. He appointed him judge-advocate of the Marshal's Office, later made him campaigning deputy of the Luolong Army, and then Commissioner for Overseeing Barbarian and Han Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天成初，偽平州節度使盧文進南歸，契丹以希崇繼其任，遣腹心總邊騎三百以監之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng the false Ping Prefecture military commissioner Lu Wenjin returned south to Jin; Khitan had Xichong succeed to his post and sent a trusted man commanding three hundred frontier horsemen to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, Lu Wenjin, the Jin-appointed military commissioner of Ping, defected south. The Khitan put Xichong in his place and sent a trusted officer with three hundred frontier horsemen to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 希崇蒞事數歲，契丹主漸加寵信。

translations.literal: After several years in office, Xichong was gradually favored and trusted by the Khitan ruler.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, the Khitan ruler came to favor and trust him more and more.

sentences.zh: 一日，登郡樓私自計曰：「昔班仲升西戍，不敢擅還，以承詔故也。

translations.literal: One day, climbing the prefectural tower, he privately reckoned: "In the past Ban Zhongsheng guarded the west and dared not return on his own, because he received an edict.
translations.idiomatic: One day he climbed the prefectural tower and thought to himself: "Long ago Ban Zhongsheng held the western frontier and dared not return without orders, because he was under imperial command.

sentences.zh: 我今入關，斷在胸臆，何恬安於不測之地而自滯耶！」

translations.literal: I now wish to enter the passes—the resolve is in my breast—why should I rest content in an uncertain land and linger of my own accord!"
translations.idiomatic: My resolve to return home is fixed in my heart. Why should I linger contentedly in this uncertain land!"

sentences.zh: 乃召漢人部曲之翹楚者，謂曰：「我陷身此地，飲酪被毛，生不見其所親，死為窮荒之鬼，南望山川，度日如歲，爾輩得無思鄉者乎！」

translations.literal: He then summoned the foremost men among his Han retainers and said: "I am trapped in this place, drinking kumiss and wearing furs; alive I do not see those I love, dead I become a ghost of the barren wilds—gazing south at mountains and rivers, each day passes like a year—can you not also be homesick!"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the leading men among his Han followers and said: "I am trapped here, drinking kumiss and wearing furs. Alive I cannot see my kin; dead I shall be a ghost of the wilderness. Gazing south at the hills and rivers, each day drags like a year. Can none of you be homesick as well?"

sentences.zh: 部曲皆泣下沾衣，且曰：「明公欲全部曲南去，善則善矣，如敵眾何？」

translations.literal: The retainers all wept until their clothes were wet and said: "If my lord wishes to take all the troops south, that would be well—but what of the enemy's numbers?
translations.idiomatic: His followers wept until their sleeves were soaked and said: "If you mean to take us all south, that would be splendid—but what of the enemy's numbers?

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》作「麾下皆言兵多不可俱亡，因勸希崇獨去。」）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History reads: "All under his command said the troops were too many to escape together and urged Xichong to go alone."))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History reads: "His commanders all said there were too many troops to escape together and urged Xichong to flee alone."))〉

sentences.zh: 希崇曰：「俟明日首領至牙帳，則先擒之，契丹無統領，其黨必散。

translations.literal: Xichong said: "Wait until tomorrow when the chieftains come to the headquarters tent, then seize them first; without Khitan leadership, their faction will surely scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong said: "Wait until tomorrow, when the chieftains come to headquarters. Seize them first. Without leaders the Khitan will scatter.

sentences.zh: 且平州去王帳千餘里，待報至征兵，逾旬方及此，則我等已入漢界深矣，何用以眾少為病！」

translations.literal: Moreover Ping Prefecture is more than a thousand li from the royal camp; waiting for reports to arrive and troops to be levied, more than ten days would pass before they reached here—by then we would already be deep within Han territory—why worry over being few against many!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Ping Prefecture is more than a thousand li from the Khitan royal camp. By the time word reached them and troops were levied, more than ten days would pass. We would already be deep inside Han territory. Why worry about being outnumbered?"

sentences.zh: 眾大喜。

translations.literal: All were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The men were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 是日，希崇於郡齋之側，坎隙地，貯石灰。

translations.literal: That day, beside the prefectural office, Xichong dug a pit in a crevice and stored quicklime.
translations.idiomatic: That day, beside the prefectural office, Xichong dug a pit in a hollow and filled it with quicklime.

sentences.zh: 明旦，首領與群從至，希崇飲以醇酎數鐘，既醉，悉投於灰阱中斃焉。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the chieftains and their followers arrived; Xichong gave them several cups of strong wine, and once drunk, cast them all into the lime pit and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the chieftains and their followers arrived. Xichong gave them several cups of strong wine, and when they were drunk he threw them all into the lime pit and killed them.

sentences.zh: 其徒營於北郭，遣人攻之，皆潰圍奔去，希崇遂以管內生口二萬餘南歸。

translations.literal: Their men were encamped outside the north wall; he sent men to attack them, and all broke the encirclement and fled; Xichong then led more than twenty thousand people within his jurisdiction south in return.
translations.idiomatic: Their men were encamped outside the north wall. He sent troops against them, and they broke out and fled. Xichong then led more than twenty thousand people under his jurisdiction back south.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗嘉之，授汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Tang Mingzong praised him and appointed him Defender of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Tang praised him and appointed him Defender of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 希崇既之任，遣人迎母赴郡。

translations.literal: Once Xichong took up his post, he sent men to welcome his mother to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up his post, Xichong sent men to bring his mother to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母及境，希崇親肩板輿行三十里，觀者無不稱嘆。

translations.literal: When his mother reached the border, Xichong personally shouldered the carrying-chair and walked thirty li; onlookers all praised and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother reached the border, Xichong personally shouldered her carrying-chair and walked thirty li. All who saw it praised him.

sentences.zh: 歷二年，遷靈州兩使留後。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to Acting Commissioner of the Two Offices at Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was made Acting Commissioner of the Two Offices at Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，靈州戍兵歲運糧經五百里，有剽攘之患。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ling Prefecture garrison troops each year transported grain over five hundred li and suffered the trouble of plunder and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Lingzhou garrison had to haul grain five hundred li each year and suffered constant raids.

sentences.zh: 希崇乃告諭邊士，廣務屯田，歲餘，軍食大濟。

translations.literal: Xichong then announced and instructed the frontier troops, broadly undertaking military colonies; after more than a year, army provisions were greatly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong then urged the frontier troops to expand military farming. Within a year the army's food supply was secure.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒之，因正授旄節。

translations.literal: An imperial letter praised him, and he was then formally granted the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised him, and he was formally granted the command baton.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，希崇厭其雜俗，頻表請覲，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era Xichong grew weary of the mixed customs and repeatedly memorialized requesting an audience; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai, Xichong grew weary of the frontier's mixed customs and repeatedly asked to come to court. An edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至闕未久，朝廷以安邊有聞，議內地處之，改邠州節度使。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching court, the court, hearing of his fame in pacifying the frontier, discussed placing him in the interior and changed him to military commissioner of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he reached court, the government, impressed by his frontier reputation, moved him inland as military commissioner of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入洛，與契丹方有要盟，慮為其所取，乃復除靈武。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he was just concluding a major alliance with Khitan and feared Xichong would be taken by them, so he again appointed him to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he was negotiating a major alliance with the Khitan and feared they might seize Xichong, so he sent him back to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 希崇嘆曰：「我應老於邊城，賦分無所逃也。」

translations.literal: Xichong sighed: "I am fated to grow old on the frontier—my allotted portion has nowhere to escape."
translations.idiomatic: Xichong sighed: "I am fated to grow old on the frontier. There is no escaping what fate has allotted me."

sentences.zh: 因郁郁不得志，久而成疾，卒於任，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Hence he was depressed and unfulfilled; after a long time he fell ill and died in office, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded in frustration, fell ill after a long spell, and died in office at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 希崇自小校累官至開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，三歷方面，封清河郡公，食邑二千戶，賜靖邊奉國忠義功臣，亦人生之榮盛者也。

translations.literal: From company officer Xichong rose through ranks to Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies and Acting Grand Marshal, held three regional commands, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and was granted the title of Meritorious Minister Loyal to the State in Pacifying the Frontier—such was also the glory of a human life.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from company officer, Xichong reached Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies and Acting Grand Marshal, held three regional commands, was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe with a fief of two thousand households, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister Loyal to the State in Pacifying the Frontier—a life's summit of honor.

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：贈太師。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History: posthumously made Grand Preceptor.))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History: posthumously made Grand Preceptor.))〉

sentences.zh: 希崇素樸厚，尤嗜書，蒞事之餘，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Xichong was by nature plain and sincere, especially fond of books; apart from official duties his hand never left the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and sincere by nature, Xichong loved books above all else and never put down a scroll when he had a spare moment from office.

sentences.zh: 不好酒樂，不蓄姬仆。

translations.literal: He did not care for wine or music and kept no concubines or servants.
translations.idiomatic: He cared nothing for wine or music and kept no concubines or personal servants.

sentences.zh: 祁寒盛暑，必儼具衣冠，廝養之輩，未嘗聞褻慢之言。

translations.literal: In bitter cold or blazing heat he always dressed in full formal attire; among grooms and servants, none ever heard an irreverent word from him.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter cold or blazing heat he always dressed in full formal attire, and none of his grooms or servants ever heard a disrespectful word from him.

sentences.zh: 事母至謹，每食必侍立，俟盥漱畢方退，物議高之。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was utmost in care; at every meal he stood in attendance and withdrew only after she had finished washing—public opinion held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with the utmost care, standing beside her at every meal until she had finished washing. Public opinion held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 性雖仁恕，或遇奸惡，則嫉之若仇。

translations.literal: Though his nature was benevolent and forgiving, when he encountered the wicked and vicious he hated them as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Though gentle and forgiving by nature, he hated the wicked as bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 在邠州日，有民與郭氏為義子，自孩提以至成人，因乖戾不受訓，遣之。

translations.literal: While at Bin Prefecture, a commoner had become an adopted son of the Guo family; from infancy to adulthood, because of perversity he would not accept instruction and was sent away.
translations.idiomatic: While at Bin, a man had been adopted by the Guo family. From childhood to adulthood he grew rebellious and would not accept discipline, so the family sent him away.

sentences.zh: 郭氏夫婦相次俱死。

translations.literal: The Guo couple died one after the other.
translations.idiomatic: The Guo couple died in succession.

sentences.zh: 郭氏有嫡子，已長，時郭氏諸親與義子相約，雲是親子，欲分其財物，助而訟之，前後數政不能理，遂成疑獄。

translations.literal: The Guo family had a legitimate son already grown; at the time Guo relatives and the adopted son agreed together, claiming he was a biological son, wishing to divide the property—they aided him in suing; several successive administrations could not settle it, and it became a doubtful case.
translations.idiomatic: The Guos had a grown legitimate son. The Guo relatives then colluded with the adopted son, claiming he was a biological son, to divide the estate. They helped him sue. Several administrations failed to settle the case, and it became a notorious doubtful suit.

sentences.zh: 希崇覽其訴，判云：「父在已離，母死不至。

translations.literal: Xichong reviewed the petition and judged: "While the father lived he left; when the mother died he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong reviewed the petition and ruled: "While his father lived he left the household; when his mother died he did not come.

sentences.zh: 正稱假子，孤二十年撫養之恩；

translations.literal: Properly called an adopted son, he abandoned twenty years of fostering grace;
translations.idiomatic: Properly speaking he was an adopted son who threw away twenty years of fostering grace;

sentences.zh: 儻曰親兒，犯三千條悖逆之罪。

translations.literal: if one claims him a biological son, he violates the three thousand statutes' crime of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: if one calls him a biological son, he commits the statutory crime of filial rebellion.

sentences.zh: 頗為傷害名教，安敢理認田園！

translations.literal: This greatly injures the norms of teaching—how dare he claim fields and gardens!
translations.idiomatic: This deeply wounds the moral order. How dare he claim the family lands!

sentences.zh: 其生涯並付親子，所訟人與朋奸者，委法官以律定刑。」

translations.literal: His livelihood and property are all given to the legitimate son; the litigant and his conspirators are entrusted to the judicial officer to fix punishment according to law."
translations.idiomatic: All property goes to the legitimate son. The litigant and his conspirators are left to the judicial officer to punish according to law."

sentences.zh: 聞者服其明。

translations.literal: Hearers admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard the ruling admired his clarity.

sentences.zh: 希崇亦善觀象，在靈州日，見月掩畢口大星，經月復爾，乃嘆曰：「畢口大星，邊將也，月再掩之，吾其終歟！」

translations.literal: Xichong was also skilled at observing omens; while at Ling Prefecture he saw the moon eclipse the great star at the mouth of the Net constellation; after a month it happened again, and he sighed: "The great star at the Net's mouth is a frontier general—the moon twice covers it; am I to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Xichong was also skilled at reading omens. At Lingzhou he saw the moon eclipse the great star at the mouth of the Net constellation, and a month later it happened again. He sighed: "That star is the star of frontier generals. The moon has covered it twice. Am I to die?"

sentences.zh: 果卒於郡。

translations.literal: He indeed died in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He did indeed die in office.

sentences.zh: 子仁謙為嗣，歷引進副使。

translations.literal: His son Renqian was heir and served as Deputy Introducing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renqian succeeded him and served as Deputy Introducing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王庭胤，字紹基，其先長安人也。

translations.literal: Wang Tingyin, courtesy name Shaoji, his ancestors were natives of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingyin, whose courtesy name was Shaoji, came from a Chang'an family.

sentences.zh: 祖處存，定州節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chucun was military commissioner of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chucun was military commissioner of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父鄴，晉州節度使。

translations.literal: His father Ye was military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye was military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庭胤，唐莊宗之內表也。

translations.literal: Tingyin was a maternal cousin of Tang Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin was a maternal cousin of Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 性勇剽狡捷，鷹瞬隼視，喑嗚眥睚，則挺劍而不顧。

translations.literal: His nature was brave, fierce, cunning, and swift; hawk-glance and falcon-stare—at a growl or a sidelong glare he would draw his sword without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Brave, fierce, cunning, and swift by nature, he had a hawk's glance and a falcon's stare. At the slightest provocation he would draw his sword without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 少為晉陽軍校，以攻城野戰為務，暑不息嘉樹之陰，寒不處密室之下，與軍伍食不異味，居不異適，故莊宗於親族之中，獨加禮遇。

translations.literal: In youth he was a company officer at Jinyang, making siege and field battle his business; in heat he did not rest in the shade of fine trees, in cold he did not dwell below a warm chamber—he ate the same fare as the ranks and lived no differently in comfort, so Zhuangzong among his kin alone showed him special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a company officer at Jinyang and devoted himself to siege and field battle. In summer he would not rest in the shade of fine trees; in winter he would not stay in a heated room. He ate the same food as the ranks and lived no more comfortably than they. Among his kin Zhuangzong singled him out for special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 莊宗、明宗朝，累歷貝、忻、密、澶、隰、相六州刺史。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Zhuangzong and Mingzong he successively held the six prefectures of Bei, Xin, Mi, Chan, Xi, and Xiang as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong and Mingzong he served in turn as prefect of Bei, Xin, Mi, Chan, Xi, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 國初，範延光據鄴稱亂，高祖以庭胤累朝宿將，詔為魏府行營中軍使兼貝州防御史。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion; Gaozu, because Tingyin was a veteran general of successive reigns, ordered him Middle Army Commander of the Ye Prefecture campaign headquarters, concurrently Defender of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Fan Yanguang rebelled and held Ye. Gaozu, regarding Tingyin as a veteran of several reigns, appointed him Middle Army Commander of the Ye campaign headquarters and Defender of Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城降賞勞，授相州節度使，尋移鎮定州。

translations.literal: When the city surrendered he was rewarded and commended, appointed military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, and soon transferred to command Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the city surrendered he was rewarded and made military commissioner of Xiang, then soon transferred to Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹欲以王處直之子威為定州節度使，處直則庭胤之叔祖也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Khitan wished to make Wang Chuzhi's son Wei military commissioner of Ding Prefecture; Chuzhi was Tingyin's great-uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had wanted to make Wang Chuzhi's son Wei military commissioner of Ding. Chuzhi was Tingyin's great-uncle.

sentences.zh: 處直為養子都所篡，時威北走契丹，契丹納之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was usurped by his adopted son Du; at the time Wei fled north to Khitan, and Khitan received him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi had been overthrown by his adopted son Du. Wei fled north to the Khitan, who took him in.

sentences.zh: 至是契丹遣使諭高祖云：「欲使王威襲先人土地，如我蕃中之制。」

translations.literal: At this time Khitan sent envoys to inform Gaozu: "We wish to have Wang Wei inherit his forebears' lands, as in our barbarian custom."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan now sent envoys to tell Gaozu: "We wish Wang Wei to inherit his forebears' lands, as is our custom."

sentences.zh: 高祖答：「以中國將校自刺史、團練、防禦使序遷，方授旄節。

translations.literal: Gaozu replied: "In China military officers are promoted in sequence from prefect, training commissioner, and defender before the command baton is granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied: "In China officers are promoted in sequence from prefect, training commissioner, and defender before the command baton is granted.

sentences.zh: 請遣威至此任用，漸令升進，乃合中土舊規。」

translations.literal: Please send Wei here for employment and gradually allow his advancement—that accords with the old rules of the central land."
translations.idiomatic: Send Wei here for employment and let him rise step by step. That accords with our old rules."

sentences.zh: 戎王深怒其見拒，使人復報曰：「爾自諸侯為天子，有何階級耶？」

translations.literal: The barbarian king was deeply angered at the refusal and sent someone to reply again: "You yourself rose from feudal lord to Son of Heaven—what rank or grade is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was furious at the refusal and sent a reply: "You yourself rose from feudal lord to Son of Heaven—what rank or grade do you speak of?"

sentences.zh: 高祖畏其滋蔓，則厚賂力拒其命。

translations.literal: Gaozu feared the trouble would spread, so with heavy bribes he strenuously refused the command.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu feared the dispute would spread, so he paid heavy bribes and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 契丹怒稍息，遂連升庭允，俾鎮中山，且欲塞其意也。

translations.literal: Khitan anger gradually subsided; Tingyin was then repeatedly promoted and made to garrison Zhongshan, also to satisfy their intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan anger gradually cooled. Tingyin was then promoted again and again and posted to garrison Zhongshan, partly to placate them.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，改滄州節度使，累官至檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was changed to military commissioner of Cang Prefecture and rose through ranks to Acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made military commissioner of Cang and eventually rose to Acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 開運元年秋，卒於位，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Kaiyun he died in office, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaiyun 1 he died in office at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有子三人，長曰昭敏，仕至金吾將軍卒。

translations.literal: He had three sons; the eldest was called Zhaomin, who served to Golden Crow General and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. The eldest, Zhaomin, rose to Golden Crow General and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史匡翰，字元輔，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Kuanghan, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kuanghan, whose courtesy name was Yuanfu, came from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 父建瑭，事莊宗為先鋒將，敵人畏之，謂之「史先鋒」，累立戰功，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Jiantang served Zhuangzong as vanguard general; enemies feared him and called him "Shi the Vanguard"; he repeatedly achieved battle merit and has a biography in the Tang History.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiantang served Zhuangzong as a vanguard general. Enemies feared him and called him "Shi the Vanguard." He won repeated battle honors and has a biography in the Tang History.

sentences.zh: 匡翰起家襲九府都督，歷代州遼州副使、檢校太子賓客。

translations.literal: Kuanghan began his career inheriting the post of Commissioner of the Nine Prefectures, served as deputy commissioner of Dai and Liao Prefectures, and Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanghan began his career by inheriting the post of Commissioner of the Nine Prefectures, then served as deputy commissioner of Dai and Liao and as Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 同光初，為嵐、憲、朔等州都遊奕使，改天雄軍牢城都指揮使，再加檢校戶部尚書，領潯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was Touring Inspector of Lan, Xian, Shuo and other prefectures, changed to Commander of the Prison City of the Tianxiong Army, then further made Acting Minister of Revenue and prefect of Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was Touring Inspector of Lan, Xian, Shuo, and other prefectures, then Commander of the Prison City of the Tianxiong Army, then Acting Minister of Revenue and prefect of Xun.

sentences.zh: 天成中，授天雄軍步軍都指揮使，歲餘，遷侍衛彰聖馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he was appointed Commander of the Tianxiong Army Foot Troops; after more than a year he became Commander of the Palace Guard Zhangsheng Horse Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was made Commander of the Tianxiong Army Foot Troops. After a year he became Commander of the Palace Guard Zhangsheng Horse Army.

sentences.zh: 高祖有天下也，授檢校司空、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu gained the realm, he was granted Acting Minister of Works and made prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu gained the realm, Kuanghan was made Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 其妻魯國長公主，即高祖之妹也。

translations.literal: His wife was the Eldest Princess of Lu, who was Gaozu's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the Eldest Princess of Lu, Gaozu's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 尋轉控鶴都指揮使兼和州刺史、駙馬都尉，俄授檢校司徒、鄭州防禦使，未幾，遷義成軍節度、滑濮等州觀察處置、管內河堤等使。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commander of the Crane-Control Army, concurrently prefect of He Prefecture and Commandant Escort, then shortly Acting Minister of Works and Defender of Zheng Prefecture; before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, Observation and Disposition Commissioner of Hua, Pu and other prefectures, and Commissioner of River Dikes within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Commander of the Crane-Control Army, concurrently prefect of He and Commandant Escort, then Acting Minister of Works and Defender of Zheng. Before long he was made military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, Observation Commissioner of Hua, Pu, and other prefectures, and Commissioner of River Dikes within the circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，尋起復本鎮。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, then soon was recalled to his former command.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother, then was soon recalled to his former command.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：陶穀撰匡翰碑文云：「圃田待理，漢殿掄才，功臣旌佐國之名，出守奉專城之寄。」

translations.literal: (Note: Tao Gu wrote Kuanghan's tomb inscription: "The garden fields await governance; the Han hall selects talent—the meritorious minister is honored with the name of aiding the state; going out to guard, he bears the charge of a walled city."
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Tao Gu wrote Kuanghan's tomb inscription: "The garden fields await governance; the Han hall selects talent—the meritorious minister is honored for aiding the state; going out to guard, he bears charge of a walled city."

sentences.zh: 蓋鄭州即在義成軍管內，匡翰雖遷官，不離本鎮也。）〉

translations.literal: For Zheng Prefecture lies within the Yicheng Army circuit; though Kuanghan changed offices, he did not leave his original command.))〉
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Prefecture lay within the Yicheng circuit, so though Kuanghan changed titles he never left his original command.))〉

sentences.zh: 匡翰剛毅有謀略，禦軍嚴整，接下以禮，與部曲語，未嘗稱名，歷數郡皆有政聲。

translations.literal: Kuanghan was resolute and had stratagems; in commanding troops he was strict and orderly; in receiving subordinates he used ritual; in speaking with retainers he never called them by personal name; through several prefectures he always had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Resolute and resourceful, Kuanghan commanded troops with strict discipline and treated subordinates with courtesy. He never addressed his retainers by personal name. In every prefecture he earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 〈（陶穀碑文云：「齋壇峻而金鼓嚴，麻案宣而油幢出。

translations.literal: (Tao Gu's tomb inscription says: "The ritual altar rises high and drums and gongs are stern; the hemp document is proclaimed and the oiled banner goes forth.
translations.idiomatic: (Tao Gu's tomb inscription says: "The ritual altar rises high and drums and gongs are stern; the hemp document is proclaimed and the oiled banner goes forth.

sentences.zh: 控梁苑之西郊，殷乎威望；

translations.literal: Holding the western suburbs of the Liang Garden, his authority was imposing;
translations.idiomatic: Holding the western suburbs of the Liang Garden, his authority was imposing;

sentences.zh: 撫國僑之遺俗，綽有政聲。」）〉

translations.literal: soothing the remnant customs of the state's expatriates, he abundantly had a reputation for governance."))〉
translations.idiomatic: soothing the remnant customs of the state's expatriates, he won abundant praise for his governance."))〉

sentences.zh: 尤好《春秋左氏傳》，每視政之暇，延學者講說，躬自執卷受業焉。

translations.literal: He especially loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; in the leisure of governing he invited scholars to lecture and explain, personally holding the scroll to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals. In his spare moments from governing he invited scholars to lecture and personally held the scroll as their student.

sentences.zh: 時發難問，窮於隱奧，流輩或戲為「史三傳」。

translations.literal: He often posed difficult questions, exhausting hidden subtleties; contemporaries jested that he was "Shi of the Three Commentaries."
translations.idiomatic: He often posed difficult questions that exhausted the text's subtleties. Contemporaries jested that he was "Shi of the Three Commentaries."

sentences.zh: 既自端謹，不喜人醉。

translations.literal: Being himself upright and careful, he did not like others to be drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and careful himself, he disliked drunkenness in others.

sentences.zh: 幕客有關徹者，狂率酣鋋。

translations.literal: Among his staff was Guan Che, wild and reckless, deep in drink.
translations.idiomatic: Among his staff was Guan Che, wild, reckless, and constantly drunk.

sentences.zh: 一日使酒，怒謂匡翰曰：「明公昔刺覃懷，與徹主客隨至，事無不可，今領節鉞，數不相容。

translations.literal: One day, drunk, he angrily told Kuanghan: "My lord once governed Tanhuai; Che followed as host and guest—nothing was refused; now holding the command baton, you repeatedly show no tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: One day, drunk, he angrily told Kuanghan: "When you governed Tanhuai, I followed you as host and guest and nothing was refused. Now that you hold the command baton, you repeatedly show me no tolerance.

sentences.zh: 且書記趙礪，險诐之人也，脅肩諂笑，黷貨無厭，而明公待之甚厚，徹今請死。

translations.literal: Moreover Secretary Zhao Li is a treacherous and deceitful man, hunching shoulders with fawning smiles, corrupt in goods without end—yet my lord treats him very generously; Che now asks to die.
translations.idiomatic: And Secretary Zhao Li is a treacherous flatterer who hunches his shoulders and smiles obsequiously and is endlessly corrupt, yet you treat him generously. I, Che, now ask to die.

sentences.zh: 近聞張彥澤臠張式，未聞匡翰斬關徹，恐天下談者未有比類。」

translations.literal: Recently I heard Zhang Yanzhe dismembered Zhang Shi, but have not heard Kuanghan execute Guan Che—I fear those who talk under heaven will find no parallel."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Zhang Yanzhe dismembered Zhang Shi, but I have not heard that you executed Guan Che. I fear the world will find no parallel for such favoritism."

sentences.zh: 匡翰不怒，引滿自罰而慰勉之，其寬厚如此。

translations.literal: Kuanghan was not angry, filled his cup to punish himself and comforted and encouraged him—such was his generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanghan was not angry. He filled his own cup as self-punishment and comforted Che. Such was his generosity.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，白馬河決，匡翰祭之，見一犬有角，浮於水心，甚惡之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu the Baima River burst its banks; Kuanghan offered sacrifice and saw a dog with horns floating at the river's center—he greatly detested the omen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 6 the Baima River burst its banks. Kuanghan offered sacrifice and saw a horned dog floating in midstream. He took the omen as a very bad sign.

sentences.zh: 後數月遘疾而卒於鎮，年四十。

translations.literal: Several months later he fell ill and died in his command, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he fell ill and died in office at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太保。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子彥容，歷宮苑使、濮單宿三州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yanrong served as Palace Parks Commissioner and prefect of Pu, Shan, and Su Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanrong served as Palace Parks Commissioner and as prefect of Pu, Shan, and Su.

sentences.zh: 楊思權，邠州新平人也。

translations.literal: Yang Siquan was a native of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Siquan came from Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化初為軍校，貞明二年，轉弓箭指揮使、檢校左僕射，累遷控鶴右第一軍使。

translations.literal: In the early Ganhuo era of Liang he was a company officer; in the second year of Zhenming he became Commander of Archers and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to Commander of the Crane-Control Army's Right First Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang's Ganhuo era he was a company officer. In Zhenming 2 he became Commander of Archers and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was eventually promoted to Commander of the Crane-Control Army's Right First Corps.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，補右廂夾馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed Commander of the Right Flank Horse-Groom Detachment.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he was appointed Commander of the Right Flank Horse-Groom Detachment.

sentences.zh: 天成初，遷右威衛將軍，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made General of the Right Weiwei Guard and given Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was made General of the Right Weiwei Guard and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 會秦王從榮鎮太原，明宗乃以馮赟為副留守、以思權為北京步軍都指揮使以佐佑之。

translations.literal: When Prince Qin Congrong garrisoned Taiyuan, Mingzong then made Feng Yun deputy garrison commander and Siquan Commander of the Northern Capital Foot Army to assist and support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qin Congrong was posted to Taiyuan, Mingzong appointed Feng Yun deputy garrison commander and made Siquan Commander of the Northern Capital Foot Army to assist him.

sentences.zh: 從榮幼驕很，不親公務，明宗乃遣紀綱一人素善從榮者，與之遊處，俾從容諷導之。

translations.literal: Congrong from youth was arrogant and harsh and did not attend to public affairs; Mingzong therefore sent a law-enforcement officer who was on good terms with Congrong to keep him company and guide him with gentle admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong had been arrogant and harsh since childhood and neglected public affairs. Mingzong therefore sent a law officer who was on good terms with him to keep him company and guide him with gentle admonition.

sentences.zh: 嘗私謂從榮曰：「河南相公恭謹好善，親禮端士，有老成之風。

translations.literal: He once privately told Congrong: "The Lord of Henan is respectful, cautious, and fond of goodness, personally honoring upright gentlemen—he has the manner of an elder statesman.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Congrong privately: "The Lord of Henan is respectful, cautious, and fond of virtue. He honors upright gentlemen and has the manner of an elder statesman.

sentences.zh: 相公處長，更宜自勵，勿致聲聞在河南之下。」

translations.literal: My lord is the elder brother—you should strive all the more and not let your reputation fall below Henan's."
translations.idiomatic: You are the elder brother and should strive all the more, so that your reputation does not fall below his."

sentences.zh: 從榮不悅，因告思權曰：「朝廷人皆推從厚，共非短我，吾將廢棄矣。」

translations.literal: Congrong was displeased and therefore told Siquan: "Everyone at court praises Conghou and together finds fault with me—I am about to be cast aside."
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was displeased and told Siquan: "Everyone at court praises Conghou and finds fault with me. I am about to be cast aside."

sentences.zh: 思權曰：「請相公勿憂，萬一有變，但思權在處有甲兵，足以濟事。」

translations.literal: Siquan said: "Please, my lord, do not worry—if anything should change, wherever Siquan is there are armored troops enough to accomplish the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Siquan said: "Do not worry, my lord. If anything should happen, wherever I am I have armored troops enough to see the matter through."

sentences.zh: 乃勸從榮招置部曲，調弓礪矢，陰為之備。

translations.literal: He then urged Congrong to recruit retainers, tune bows and sharpen arrows, and secretly make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Congrong to recruit retainers, tune bows, sharpen arrows, and make secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 思權又謂使者曰：「朝廷教君伴相公，終日言弟賢兄弱何也？

translations.literal: Siquan also told the envoy: "The court ordered you to accompany my lord—why do you speak all day of the younger brother's worth and the elder brother's weakness?
translations.idiomatic: Siquan also told the envoy: "The court ordered you to keep my lord company. Why do you speak all day of the younger brother's worth and the elder brother's weakness?

sentences.zh: 吾輩茍在，豈不能與相公為主耶？」

translations.literal: If we are still alive, can we not make my lord ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: As long as we live, can we not make my lord ruler?"

sentences.zh: 使者懼，告馮赟，乃密奏之。

translations.literal: The envoy was afraid, told Feng Yun, and secretly memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was frightened, told Feng Yun, and secretly reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃詔思權赴京師，以秦王之故，亦弗之罪也。

translations.literal: Mingzong then ordered Siquan to come to the capital; for the Prince of Qin's sake he also did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then ordered Siquan to the capital. For the Prince of Qin's sake he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 長興末，為右羽林都指揮使，遣戍興元。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing he was Commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army and was sent to garrison Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changxing he was made Commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army and sent to garrison Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，奉詔從張虔釗討鳳翔，洎至岐下，思權首倡倒戈以攻虔釗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, he followed an edict with Zhang Qianjiao to campaign against Fengxiang; when they reached Qi, Siquan was first to urge turning spears to attack Qianjiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded, Siquan followed an edict with Zhang Qianjiao to campaign against Fengxiang. At Qi he was the first to turn his troops against Qianjiao.

sentences.zh: 尋領部下軍率先入城，謂唐末帝曰：「臣既赤心奉殿下，俟京城平定，與臣一鎮，勿置在防禦團練使內。」

translations.literal: Soon leading his troops he was first to enter the city and told the Last Emperor of Tang: "Your servant has served Your Highness with a loyal heart—when the capital is pacified, grant me one command; do not place me among defenders and training commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: He soon led his troops into the city first and told the Last Emperor of Tang: "I have served Your Highness with a loyal heart. When the capital is pacified, grant me a regional command. Do not rank me among defenders and training commissioners."

sentences.zh: 乃懷中出紙一幅，謂末帝曰：「願殿下親書臣姓名以誌之。」

translations.literal: He then drew a sheet of paper from his breast and told the Last Emperor: "I wish Your Highness would personally write my name to record it."
translations.idiomatic: He then drew a sheet of paper from his breast and said: "I ask Your Highness to write my name yourself as a record."

sentences.zh: 末帝命筆，書「可邠寧節度使」。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor ordered brush and wrote "May be military commissioner of Bin and Ning."
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor took up the brush and wrote: "May be military commissioner of Bin and Ning."

sentences.zh: 及即位，授推誠奉國保乂功臣、靜難軍節度、邠寧慶衍等州觀察處置等使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Siquan was granted the title Meritorious Minister Sincere in Devotion Who Preserves the State, military commissioner of the Jingnan Army, Observation and Disposition Commissioner of Bin, Ning, Qing, Yan and other prefectures, and Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Siquan was granted the title Meritorious Minister Sincere in Devotion Who Preserves the State, made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army and Observation Commissioner of Bin, Ning, Qing, Yan, and other prefectures, and Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 清泰三年，入為右龍武軍統軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingtai he entered the court as Commander-in-Chief of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 3 he was made Commander-in-Chief of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，除左衛上將軍，進封開國公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made General of the Left Guard and advanced to Duke of the State-Founding.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made General of the Left Guard and advanced to Duke of the State-Founding.

sentences.zh: 天福八年，以疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 8 he died of illness at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子勛，事皇朝，累歷軍職，遷內外馬步都軍頭，見為郢州防禦使。

translations.literal: His son Xun served the imperial court, passed through many military posts, rose to Commander of All Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies, and at present is Defender of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun served the dynasty through many military posts, rose to Commander of All Inner and Outer Horse and Foot Armies, and at the time of writing was Defender of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李從璋，字子良，後唐明宗皇帝之猶子也。

translations.literal: Li Congzhang, courtesy name Ziliang, was a nephew of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congzhang, whose courtesy name was Ziliang, was a nephew of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，從明宗歷戰河上，有平梁之功。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at riding and archery; he followed Mingzong through battles on the Yellow River and had merit in pacifying Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was skilled at riding and archery. He followed Mingzong through the battles along the Yellow River and helped pacify Liang.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，魏之亂軍迎明宗為帝，從璋時引軍自常山過邢，邢人以從璋為留後。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang of Tang, Wei's mutinous troops welcomed Mingzong as emperor; Congzhang then led troops from Changshan through Xing, and the people of Xing made Congzhang acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang's Tongguang era, Wei's mutinous troops welcomed Mingzong as emperor. Congzhang led troops from Changshan through Xing, and the people of Xing made him acting commander.

sentences.zh: 逾月，明宗即位，受詔領捧聖左廂都指揮使，時天成元年五月也。

translations.literal: After more than a month Mingzong took the throne; he received an edict to command the Left Flank of the Sacred Guard Army—it was the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Mingzong took the throne and ordered him to command the Left Flank of the Sacred Guard Army. It was the fifth month of Tiancheng 1.

sentences.zh: 八月，改大內皇城使，加檢校司徒、彰國軍節度使，賜竭忠建策興復功臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was changed to Commissioner of the Inner Imperial City, given Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army, and granted the title Meritorious Minister Exhausting Loyalty in Planning Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became Commissioner of the Inner Imperial City, Acting Minister of Works, and military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army, and received the title Meritorious Minister Exhausting Loyalty in Planning Restoration.

sentences.zh: 旋以達靼諸部入寇，從璋率麾下出討，一鼓而破，有詔褒之。
