translations.literal: Soon the Dadan tribes and others invaded; Congzhang led his followers out to campaign, broke them in one assault, and received an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Dadan tribes and others invaded. Congzhang led his men out, broke them in one assault, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，移鎮滑臺。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he transferred to command Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he was transferred to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 時明宗駐蹕於大梁，從璋嘗召幕客謀曰：「車駕省方，藩臣咸有進獻，吾為臣為子，安得後焉。

translations.literal: At the time Mingzong was sojourning at Daliang; Congzhang once summoned his staff to plot: "The imperial carriage is touring the realm—all feudal ministers are making offerings. As subject and son, how can I come last?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then sojourning at Daliang. Congzhang once summoned his staff and said: "The emperor is touring the realm and every feudal minister is making offerings. As subject and son, how can I come last?

sentences.zh: 欲取倉廩羨余，以助其用。

translations.literal: I wish to take the surplus from the granaries to assist his expenses.
translations.idiomatic: I want to take surplus grain from the granaries to help with his expenses.

sentences.zh: 諸君以為何如？」

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 內有賓介白曰：「聖上寬而難犯，行宮在近，忽致上達，則一幕俱罹其罪。」

translations.literal: Among them a guest-adviser spoke: "The sage ruler is lenient yet hard to offend; the traveling palace is near—if this suddenly reaches him, the whole staff will suffer punishment together."
translations.idiomatic: One guest-adviser said: "The emperor is lenient but not to be offended. His traveling palace is near. If this reaches him, the whole staff will suffer together."

sentences.zh: 從璋怒。

translations.literal: Congzhang was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang was furious.

sentences.zh: 翌日，欲引弓射所言者，朝廷知之，改授右驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: The next day he wished to draw his bow and shoot the one who had spoken; the court learned of it and changed him to General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he wanted to shoot the man who had spoken. When the court learned of it, he was made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 長興元年十月，出鎮陜州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Changxing he went out to command Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Changxing 1 he was posted to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，遷河中節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year he was transferred to military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he was made military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 三年，就加檢校太傅，賜忠勤靜理崇義功臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title Acting Grand Tutor and granted the title Meritorious Minister Loyal, Diligent, Calm in Governance, and Honoring Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor and the honorific Meritorious Minister Loyal, Diligent, Calm in Governance, and Honoring Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，制封洋王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was enfeoffed by edict as Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，明宗厭代，閔帝嗣位，尋受命代潞王於岐上，會潞王舉兵入洛，事遂寢。

translations.literal: That year Mingzong died; Emperor Min succeeded; soon he received orders to replace the Prince of Lu at Qi—but when the Prince of Lu raised troops and entered Luoyang, the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mingzong died and Emperor Min succeeded. Congzhang was soon ordered to replace the Prince of Lu at Qi, but when the prince raised troops and entered Luoyang the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之元年十二月，授威勝軍節度使，降封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Gaozu's accession he was appointed military commissioner of the Weisheng Army and demoted to Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Gaozu's first year he was made military commissioner of the Weisheng Army and demoted to Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，終於任，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year he died in office, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year he died in office at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 鄧人為之罷市，思遺愛也。

translations.literal: The people of Deng closed their markets for him, remembering his lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Deng closed their markets in mourning, remembering his kindness.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 從璋性貪黷，懼明宗嚴正，自滑帥入居環衛之後，以除拜差跌，心稍悛悟，後歷數鎮，與故時幕客不足者相遇，無所憾焉。

translations.literal: Congzhang's nature was greedy and corrupt; he feared Mingzong's severity—after entering the palace guard from command at Hua, because of demotions in appointments his heart gradually repented; later through several commands, when he met former staff who had been slighted, he harbored no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang was greedy and corrupt by nature and feared Mingzong's severity. After he entered the palace guard from his post at Hua, repeated demotions gradually sobered him. Later, when he met former staff he had slighted, he bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 蒲、陜之日，政有善譽，改賜「忠勤靜理」之號，良以此也。

translations.literal: During his days at Pu and Shan his governance had a good reputation; the title "Loyal, Diligent, Calm in Governance" was changed and granted—truly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: At Pu and Shan his governance won a good reputation, which is why he received the revised title Loyal, Diligent, and Calm in Governance.

sentences.zh: 及高祖在位，愈畏其法，故歿於南陽，人甚惜之，亦明宗宗室之白眉也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was on the throne he feared the law all the more; thus he died at Nanyang and people greatly regretted it—he was also the white eyebrow among Mingzong's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he feared the law all the more. When he died at Nanyang many regretted it. He was the outstanding man among Mingzong's clan.

sentences.zh: 子重俊。

translations.literal: His son was Chongjun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chongjun.

sentences.zh: 重俊，唐長興、清泰中，歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Chongjun, in Changxing and Qingtai of Tang, passed through the various guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun served through the various guard generalships during Tang's Changxing and Qingtai eras.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，遙領池州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he held titular command as prefect of Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he held a titular commission as prefect of Chi.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，授虢州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was appointed prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 性貪鄙，常為郡人所訟，下御史臺，抵贓至重，太后以猶子之故救之，乃歸罪於判官高獻，止罷其郡。

translations.literal: His nature was greedy and base; he was often sued by people of the prefecture, sent down to the Censorate, and the embezzlement proved very heavy—the Empress Dowager saved him for being a nephew, and blame was placed on judge-advocate Gao Xian; he was only removed from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and base by nature, he was often sued by the people of his prefecture. The case went to the Censorate and the embezzlement was grave. The Empress Dowager saved him as a nephew, blame was shifted to his judge-advocate Gao Xian, and he was merely removed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復居環列，出典商州。

translations.literal: Before long he again joined the palace guard ranks and went out to govern Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rejoined the palace guard and was sent out to govern Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 商民素貧，重俊臨之，割剝幾盡。

translations.literal: The people of Shang were always poor; under Chongjun's rule they were exploited almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shang were always poor. Under Chongjun they were exploited almost to the last penny.

sentences.zh: 復禦家不法，其奴仆若履湯蹈火，忤其意者，或鞭之，或刃之。

translations.literal: He also ruled his household lawlessly; his servants were as if treading boiling water or walking through fire—those who offended him were sometimes whipped, sometimes cut down.
translations.idiomatic: He also ruled his household lawlessly. His servants lived as if on boiling coals. Those who offended him were whipped or killed.

sentences.zh: 又殺從人孫漢榮，掠其妻。

translations.literal: He also killed his follower Sun Hanrong and seized his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed his follower Sun Hanrong and seized Hanrong's wife.

sentences.zh: 及受代歸洛，漢榮母燕氏獲其子婦，以訴於府尹景延廣。

translations.literal: When he was relieved and returned to Luoyang, Hanrong's mother Lady Yan obtained her daughter-in-law and brought suit to Prefect Jing Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: When he was relieved and returned to Luoyang, Hanrong's mother Lady Yan recovered her daughter-in-law and sued Prefect Jing Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 牙將張守英謂燕曰：「重俊前朝枝葉，今上中表，河南尹其何以理？

translations.literal: Staff officer Zhang Shouying told Yan: "Chongjun is a branch of the former dynasty and a cousin of the present emperor—how can the Lord of Henan judge this?
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Zhang Shouying told Yan: "Chongjun is kin to the former dynasty and a cousin of the present emperor. How can the Lord of Henan judge this case?

sentences.zh: 不若邀其金帛，私自和解，策之上也。」

translations.literal: Better to demand gold and silk from him and settle privately—that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: Better to demand gold and silk and settle privately. That is the best course."

sentences.zh: 燕從其言，授三百緡而止。

translations.literal: Yan followed his words, received three hundred strings of cash, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yan followed his advice, accepted three hundred strings of cash, and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 後以青衣趙滿師因不勝楚毒，逾垣訴景延廣，雲重俊與妹私奸及前後不法事，延廣奏之。

translations.literal: Later the maid Zhao Manshi, unable to bear the flogging, climbed the wall and appealed to Jing Yanguang, saying Chongjun had committed incest with his sister and other unlawful acts before and after; Yanguang memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the maid Zhao Manshi, unable to bear the flogging, climbed the wall and appealed to Jing Yanguang, reporting Chongjun's incest with his sister and other crimes. Yanguang memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔遣刑部郎中王瑜鞫之，盡得其實，並以穢跡彰露，而賜死於家。

translations.literal: An edict sent Ministry of Justice Director Wang Yu to investigate; the facts were fully obtained, and because the foul deeds were exposed, he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Ministry of Justice Director Wang Yu to investigate. The facts were fully established and the foul deeds exposed. Chongjun was granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 李從溫，字德基，代州崞縣人，後唐明宗之猶子也。

translations.literal: Li Congwen, courtesy name Deji, was a native of Guo County in Dai Prefecture, a nephew of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congwen, whose courtesy name was Deji, came from Guo County in Dai Prefecture and was a nephew of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗微時，從溫執仆禦之役，後養為己子。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was still obscure, Congwen performed the duties of a servant and groom; later he was adopted as his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was still obscure, Congwen served him as a servant and groom. Later Mingzong adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 及歷諸藩，署為牙校，命典廄庫。

translations.literal: When he passed through the various feudal commands, he was appointed gate officer and ordered to manage the stables and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: As Mingzong passed through the various commands, he appointed Congwen a gate officer and put him in charge of the stables and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，奏授銀青光祿大夫、檢校右散騎常侍，累加檢校司空，充北京副留守。

translations.literal: In Tongguang of Tang he was memorialized and granted Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Right Regular Attendant, then repeatedly given Acting Minister of Works and made Deputy Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tongguang era he was granted Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Right Regular Attendant, then Acting Minister of Works and Deputy Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，授安國節度使、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was appointed military commissioner of the Anguo Army and Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, he was made military commissioner of the Anguo Army and Acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 長興元年四月，入為右武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Changxing he entered the court as General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Changxing 1 he was made General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復出鎮許田。

translations.literal: That year he again went out to command Xutian.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was again posted to command Xutian.

sentences.zh: 明年，移北京留守，加太傅。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital and given Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，改太平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was changed to military commissioner of the Taiping Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he was made military commissioner of the Taiping Army.

sentences.zh: 五月，制封兗王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was enfeoffed by edict as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，移鎮定州，兼北面行營副招討使，尋又移鎮常山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he transferred to command Ding Prefecture, concurrently Deputy Campaign Commissioner of the Northern Frontier, and soon again transferred to command Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Ding Prefecture as Deputy Campaign Commissioner of the Northern Frontier, and soon afterward to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，加同平章事，改鎮彭門。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he was given Associate Grand Councilor and changed to command Peng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was made Associate Grand Councilor and transferred to Peng Gate.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之明年，就加侍中。

translations.literal: In the year after Gaozu's accession he was given Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Gaozu's accession he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given concurrent Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made concurrent Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八年，再為許州節度使、開府儀同三司，封趙國公，累加食邑一萬戶，食實封一千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again became military commissioner of Xu Prefecture and Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and repeatedly given a fief of ten thousand households with actual enfeoffment of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again became military commissioner of Xu, Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and Duke of Zhao, with a nominal fief of ten thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of twelve hundred.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，改河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was changed to military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 2 he was made military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，卒於任，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he died in office, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he died in office at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，追封隴西郡王。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and retroactively enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and retroactively enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 從溫始以明宗本枝，歷居藩翰，無文武才略資濟代之用，凡臨民以貨利為急。

translations.literal: Congwen began as a branch of Mingzong's house, passed through regional commands, had no civil or military talent or stratagem to aid the age, and whenever governing the people made profit his urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen was a branch of Mingzong's house and held several regional commands, but he had no civil or military talent to serve the age. Whenever he governed the people, profit came first.

sentences.zh: 在常山日，睹牙署池潭凡十餘頃，皆立木為岸，而以修篁環之，從溫曰：「此何用為？」

translations.literal: While at Changshan he saw the headquarters ponds and pools totaling more than ten qing, all with timber set as banks and fine bamboo surrounding them; Congwen said: "What use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: At Changshan he saw the headquarters ponds, more than ten qing in all, timbered banks ringed with fine bamboo. He said: "What use is all this?"

sentences.zh: 悉命伐竹取木，鬻於列肆，獲其直以實用帑焉。

translations.literal: He ordered all the bamboo cut and timber taken, sold in the market stalls, and the proceeds used to fill the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all the bamboo cut and the timber taken, sold in the markets, and the proceeds poured into his treasury.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，從溫時在兗州，多創乘輿器服，為宗族切戒，從溫弗聽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Congwen was then at Yan Prefecture and made many imperial carriage utensils and robes; the clan urgently warned him, but Congwen would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Congwen was at Yan and had many imperial carriage utensils and robes made. His clan urgently warned him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其妻關氏，素耿介，一日厲聲於牙門云：「李從溫欲為亂，擅造天子法物。」

translations.literal: His wife Lady Guan was always upright; one day she shouted sharply at the headquarters gate: "Li Congwen wishes to rebel and has presumptuously made the Son of Heaven's ritual objects."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Guan was upright by nature. One day she shouted at the headquarters gate: "Li Congwen is plotting rebellion and has presumptuously made imperial ritual objects."

sentences.zh: 從溫敬謝，悉命焚之，家無敗累，關氏之力也。

translations.literal: Congwen respectfully apologized and ordered them all burned; the household escaped ruin—this was Lady Guan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen apologized respectfully and had them all burned. The household escaped ruin thanks to Lady Guan.

sentences.zh: 後以多畜駝馬，縱牧近郊，民有訴其害稼者，從溫曰：「若從爾之意，則我產畜何歸乎？」

translations.literal: Later because he kept many camels and horses and let them graze in the near suburbs, when the people complained that they harmed the crops, Congwen said: "If I follow your wishes, where will my livestock go?"
translations.idiomatic: Later he kept many camels and horses and let them graze in the suburbs. When people complained that they were ruining the crops, Congwen said: "If I do as you wish, where will my livestock go?"

sentences.zh: 其昏愚多此類也。

translations.literal: His stupidity was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His folly was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 高祖性至察，知而不問。

translations.literal: Gaozu's nature was extremely observant—he knew but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was extremely observant. He knew but did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，太后教曰：「吾只有此兄，慎勿繩之。」

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, the Empress Dowager instructed: "I have only this elder brother—be careful not to bind him."
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, the Empress Dowager instructed: "I have only this elder brother. Be careful not to punish him."

sentences.zh: 故愈加姑息，以致年逾耳順，終於牖下，乃天幸也。

translations.literal: Hence he was indulged all the more, so that past the age of sixty he ended beneath his own roof—it was heaven's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he was indulged all the more, so that he lived past sixty and died in his own house. That was heaven's mercy.

sentences.zh: 張萬進，突厥南鄙人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanjin was from the southern marches of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wanjin came from the southern marches of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 祖拽斤，父臘。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Zhuaijin; his father was La.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Zhuaijin and his father La.

sentences.zh: 萬進白皙美髯，少而無賴。

translations.literal: Wanjin was fair-skinned with a fine beard and was a ruffian in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin was fair-skinned with a fine beard and was a ruffian in his youth.

sentences.zh: 事唐武皇，以騎射著名，攻城野戰，奮不顧命。

translations.literal: He served Tang's Martial Emperor, was famous for riding and archery, and in siege and field battle fought without regard for his life.
translations.idiomatic: He served Tang's Martial Emperor and was famous for horsemanship and archery. In siege and field battle he fought without regard for his life.

sentences.zh: 嘗與梁軍對陣，持銳首短刀，躍馬獨進，及兵刃既刓，則易以大錘，左右奮擊，出沒進退，無敢當者。

translations.literal: Once facing the Liang army in formation, he held a sharp-headed short blade, leaped his horse and advanced alone; when the weapons were worn down he switched to a great hammer, striking fiercely left and right, appearing and vanishing, advancing and retreating—none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Once facing the Liang army, he charged alone with a sharp-headed short blade. When his weapons wore down he switched to a great hammer, striking left and right as he charged in and out. None dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗、明宗素憐其雄勇，復獎其戰功，故累典大郡。

translations.literal: Tang's Zhuangzong and Mingzong always pitied his fierce courage and also rewarded his battle merit, so he repeatedly held great prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Tang admired his fierce courage and rewarded his battle merit, so he repeatedly held major commands.

sentences.zh: 天成、長興中，歷威勝、保大兩鎮節制。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng and Changxing he held command of the Weisheng and Baoda circuits.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng and Changxing he commanded the Weisheng and Baoda circuits.

sentences.zh: 高祖有天下，命為彰義軍節度使，所至不治，政由群下。

translations.literal: When Gaozu gained the realm, he was ordered military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army; wherever he went he did not govern—affairs were left to his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu gained the realm, he was made military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army. Wherever he went he did not govern, leaving affairs to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 洎至涇原，兇恣彌甚。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingyuan, his ferocity and license grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jingyuan, his cruelty and license grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 每日於公庭列大鼎，烹肥寧，割胾方寸以啖賓佐，皆流淚不能大嚼，俟其他顧，則致袂中。

translations.literal: Every day in the public court he set out great cauldrons, boiled rich meat, cut cubes an inch square to feed his guests and staff—they all wept and could not chew greatly; waiting until he looked elsewhere, they tucked the meat into their sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Every day in the public hall he set out great cauldrons of rich meat, cut it into inch cubes, and forced his guests and staff to eat. They wept and could not swallow. When he looked away, they hid the meat in their sleeves.

sentences.zh: 又命巨觶行酒，訴則辱之，乃有持杯偽飲，褰領裱而納之者。

translations.literal: He also ordered huge goblets for serving wine; if one complained he shamed him—thus some held the cup and pretended to drink, lifting the collar lining and tucking the meat inside.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered huge goblets for serving wine. Anyone who protested was shamed. Some pretended to drink, then lifted their collar linings and hid the meat inside.

sentences.zh: 既沈湎無節，唯婦言是用，其妻與幕使張光載干預公政，納錢數萬，補一豪民為捕賊將，領兵數百人入新平郡境。

translations.literal: Once sunk in drink without restraint, he followed only his wife's words; his wife and staff envoy Zhang Guangzai interfered in public affairs, took tens of thousands in cash, and appointed a powerful local man as bandit-catcher general, leading several hundred troops into the border of Xinping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in drink without restraint, he followed only his wife's counsel. She and his staff envoy Zhang Guangzai interfered in government, took tens of thousands in cash, and appointed a local magnate bandit-catcher general with several hundred troops to enter Xinping.

sentences.zh: 邠帥以其事上奏，有詔詰之，光載坐流罪，配於登州。

translations.literal: The Bin commander memorialized the matter; an edict interrogated them; Guangzai was convicted of exile and assigned to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin commander reported the matter. An edict ordered an inquiry. Guangzai was convicted of exile and sent to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天福四年三月，萬進疾篤，月餘，州兵將亂，乃詔副使萬庭圭委其符印。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Tianfu Wanjin was gravely ill; after more than a month the prefectural troops were about to mutiny, so an edict ordered Vice Commissioner Wan Tinggui to take over his seals and tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianfu 4, Wanjin fell gravely ill. After more than a month the garrison was near mutiny, and an edict ordered Vice Commissioner Wan Tinggui to take over his seals and tallies.

sentences.zh: 記室李升素憾淩虐，知其將亡，謂庭圭曰：「氣息將奄，不保晨暮，促移就第，豈不宜乎！」

translations.literal: Recorder Li Sheng had long resented the bullying and cruelty; knowing Wanjin would die, he told Tinggui: "His breath is about to fail—he may not last from morning to evening; urge him to move to his residence—is that not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Li Sheng had long resented Wanjin's bullying. Knowing he would die, he told Tinggui: "His breath is failing and he may not last the day. Urge him to move to his residence. Would that not be fitting?"

sentences.zh: 庭圭從之。

translations.literal: Tinggui followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui did so.

sentences.zh: 萬進尋卒，遂以籃轝秘屍而出，即馳騎而奏之，詔命既至，而後發喪。

translations.literal: Wanjin soon died; they then carried the corpse out secretly in a basket litter, immediately sent riders to report it, and only after the edict arrived did they proclaim mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin soon died. They secretly carried his body out in a basket litter, sent riders at once to report it, and proclaimed mourning only after the edict arrived.

sentences.zh: 其妻素很戾，謂長子彥球曰：「萬庭圭逼迫危病，驚擾而死，不手戮之，奚為生也！」

translations.literal: His wife was always harsh and violent; she told the eldest son Yanqiu: "Wan Tinggui pressed upon a man in critical illness and startled him to death—if I do not kill him with my own hand, why should I live!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife was harsh and violent by nature. She told her eldest son Yanqiu: "Wan Tinggui harassed a dying man and startled him to death. If I do not kill him myself, why should I live?"

sentences.zh: 庭圭聞之，不敢往吊。

translations.literal: When Tinggui heard this, he dared not go to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinggui heard this, he dared not attend the mourning.

sentences.zh: 萬進假殯於精舍之下，至彗東轅，凡數月之間，郡民數萬，無一饋奠者。

translations.literal: Wanjin's temporary lying-in-state was below a monastery; until the comet reached the eastern shaft—in all, over several months among tens of thousands of people in the commandery, not one offered funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin's body lay in temporary state below a monastery. For several months, among tens of thousands in the commandery, not one person brought funeral offerings.

sentences.zh: 為不善者，眾必棄之，信矣夫！

translations.literal: One who does evil—the multitude is sure to abandon him—truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Those who do evil are surely abandoned by the multitude. How true that is!

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：延廣功扶二帝，任掌六師，亦可謂晉之勛臣矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yanguang's merit supported two emperors and he held command of the Six Armies—he may also be called a meritorious minister of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yanguang's merit supported two emperors and he commanded the Six Armies. He may be called a meritorious minister of Jin.

sentences.zh: 然而昧經國之遠圖，肆狂言於強敵，卒使邦家蕩覆，宇縣丘墟，《書》所謂「惟口起羞」者，其斯人之謂歟！

translations.literal: Yet he was ignorant of the far-reaching plans for governing the state, let loose mad words before a strong enemy, and in the end caused the realm to be overturned and the counties and districts reduced to ruins—is this not what the Documents means by "from the mouth comes shame"!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked vision for governing the state, hurled mad words at a powerful enemy, and in the end brought the realm to ruin. Is this not what the Documents means by "from the mouth comes shame"?

sentences.zh: 彥韜既負且乘，任重才微，盜斯奪之，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Yantao both bore a burden and rode atop it—heavy responsibility with slight talent; the thief then seized it from him—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yantao bore a burden he could not carry and talent unequal to his post. That a thief should seize his place was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 希崇蔚有雄幹，老於塞垣，未盡其才，良亦可惜。

translations.literal: Xichong abundantly had heroic capacity and grew old on the frontier walls—his talent was not fully used; truly this is also regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong had abundant ability and grew old on the frontier. That his talent was not fully used is truly regrettable.

sentences.zh: 楊、尹二將，因倒戈而仗鉞，豈義士之所為！

translations.literal: The two generals Yang and Yin, by turning their spears gained command of the battle-axe—is this what a man of righteousness would do!
translations.idiomatic: Generals Yang and Yin won command by turning their spears against their own side. Is that the act of righteous men?

sentences.zh: 其餘蓋以勛以親，鹹分屏翰，唯萬進之醜德，又何暇於譏焉！

translations.literal: The rest were mostly honored for merit or kinship and all shared in regional defense—only Wanjin's foul virtue—who has leisure to criticize that!
translations.idiomatic: The rest were honored for merit or kinship and shared in guarding the realm. Only Wanjin's foul conduct—who has time to dwell on that!
